deadline.value: Applications open in October and are accepted all year; funding decisions run December to April, so apply October to March. For the President's PhD Scholarship (open to all nationalities) the rounds close 2 Nov 2026, 11 Jan 2027 and 1 Mar 2027 (23:59 UK time).
deadline.quote: Applications open in October, and then are accepted throughout the year. Funding decisions are typically made starting in December and ending in April. For applicants requiring funding, we recommend that you apply early (October to March) to increase the chances of securing supervision and funding.

also.quote: Applicants who apply by 23:59 (UK time) 2 November 2026 and are awarded a scholarship will be notified by 31 January 2027. | Applicants who apply by 23:59 (UK time) 11 January 2027 | Applicants who apply by 23:59 (UK time) 1 March 2027

supervisor.value: You are strongly encouraged to contact potential supervisors first and name one who agrees. You can apply without one (choosing Pure, Applied, Stats or Mathematical Finance), but such pooled applications are less likely to succeed.
supervisor.quote: Before you submit your formal application to Imperial, we strongly encourage you to contact the academic staff members with whom you would like to work to discuss your proposed research project and check whether they are planning to take on new PhD students. | If you are unable to find an academic who is happy for you to indicate their name as prospective supervisor on your online application, you can still apply without naming a supervisor.

funding.value: The department normally makes offers only to applicants who have secured funding. Every application is considered automatically for department and Imperial scholarships, but very few go to overseas students: the EPSRC DTP normally funds about one overseas student a year, and Roth awards may cover only part of an overseas fee.
funding.quote: Please note that we normally only make offers for admission to applicants who secured funding.

also.quote: All applications made via the Imperial online application system My Imperial are automatically considered for department/Imperial scholarship schemes.
Normally, one outstanding overseas applicant per year might be offered this scholarship (subject to Imperial's total grant allocation).

entry_route.value: You need a first or 2:1 honours bachelor's degree plus a master's (or a first or 2:1 integrated master's) in maths, physics, computer science, statistics or a similar subject.
entry_route.quote: A first or upper second -class honours degree (or equivalent from a non-UK University) and a master’s degree in relevant subjects such as Mathematics, Physics, Computer Sciences, Statistics.

toefl_min.value: Mathematics requires Imperial's Standard English level: TOEFL iBT 92 overall (min 20 in each section), or 4.5 on the new scale.
toefl_min.quote: Students are required to achieve Imperial’s Standard level of attainment in English language before registration.

ielts_min.value: Mathematics requires Imperial's Standard English level: IELTS Academic 6.5 overall (min 6.0 in each element).
ielts_min.quote: Students are required to achieve Imperial’s Standard level of attainment in English language before registration.

notes: Apply to Mathematics Research (PhD) via My Imperial and name a stream: Pure, Applied, Statistics or Mathematical Finance. Statistics PhDs are part of this programme. Most non-EEA nationals, including Indians, need ATAS clearance after an offer. A research proposal is optional except for President's Scholarship applicants. Centres for Doctoral Training have their own application processes.
